items.title: Strike action at Diageo site suspended ahead of talks
items.summary: Strike action at a Diageo site in Scotland has been shelved ahead of talks between the spirits giant and union officials.

items.title: Nestlé doubles investment in Mexico to $2B
items.summary: The Nescafé maker said the additional $1 billion will allow the food giant to tap into the country’s growth opportunities.

items.title: Spain snacks group Apex buys local distributor Industrias Marjo
items.summary: Spanish snacks major Grupo Apex has moved to grow its presence in the country’s convenience market with the acquisition of a local distributor. The post Spain snacks group Apex buys local distributor Industrias Marjo appeared first on Just Food .

items.title: Eduardo López-Puertas Transitions To Role Of Metro Serbia CEO From Makro Spain
items.summary: Eduardo López-Puertas has been appointed general manager (CEO) of Metro Serbia, as it marks over two decades of activity.

items.title: CEO Sander van der Laan is leaving Douglas; Jean-Marc Bellaiche will succeed him
items.summary: After a 36-year career in international retail, including 4 years at Douglas, Sander van der Laan is stepping down from his position. Jean-Marc Bellaiche of France has been appointed CEO effective November 1 for a four-year term.

items.title: IT outages at Ahold Delhaize may last another week
items.summary: On Wednesday morning, the effects of the cyber incident at Ahold Delhaize were still being felt. According to European executive Margaret Versteden-van Duijn, it will take “a few days to a week” for everything to be restored.

items.title: The Netherlands halts expansion of store hours: municipalities get to choose
items.summary: The Netherlands is abandoning the idea of further relaxing store hours. The government is sticking to the current Store Hours Act and leaving it up to municipalities to decide how long stores may remain open on Sundays and holidays. Meanwhile, Belgium is moving in the opposite…

items.title: Court agrees with former Jumbo CEO Frits van Eerd: further investigation is needed
items.summary: A boost for former Jumbo CEO Frits van Eerd: on appeal, the court of appeals has granted virtually all of his lawyers’ requests. The Public Prosecutor’s Office must produce hundreds of missing documents and call new witnesses.

items.title: Culina Unites Under One Brand Identity
items.summary: Culina Group, a third-party logistics and supply chain specialist in the UK and Ireland, and its subsidiaries are uniting under a single identity: Culina.

items.title: [Analysis] Non-European marketplaces are more dominant than ever in European e-commerce
items.summary: Non-European marketplaces are attracting an increasingly large share of international e-commerce. Among the 100 largest platforms, nearly 80% of trading volume now comes from cross-border transactions. Amazon, Temu, and AliExpress lead the market.

items.title: German Inflation Rises To Highest Level In 2026 – Destatis
items.summary: The inflation rate in Germany rose to its highest level in 2026, standing at 3.3% in September, according to data from the Federal Statistical Office.

items.title: Colruyt Group In Talks With Carrefour To Sell Wholesaler Codifrance
items.summary: Colruyt Group has initiated exclusive negotiations with retail giant Carrefour regarding the potential sale of Codifrance.

items.title: Hijos de Rivera sets up Germany subsidiary
items.summary: Spanish brewer Corporación Hijos de Rivera, the parent of Estrella Galicia, has expanded its international footprint with a subsidiary in Germany.

items.title: German government backs sugar tax plan
items.summary: Germany's federal cabinet has approved draft legislation for a tax on the sugar content of drinks sold in the country.

items.title: Kaufland Romania Introduces Beauty Zone Concept
items.summary: Kaufland Romania has launched a pilot in-store beauty and personal care section at its store on Barbu Văcărescu Street in Bucharest.

items.title: Stuck Between Seasons, UK Consumers Continue Cautious Spending – NIQ
items.summary: UK consumer spending continued to cool, as major supermarkets’ till sales rose by 1.4% in the four weeks to 3 October, notes NIQ.

items.title: Colruyt Group refers to Ahold Delhaize cyber incident in an advert
items.summary: The cyber incidents at Ahold Delhaize and in French supermarkets have inspired Collect&Go: the Colruyt Group’s grocery delivery service is playfully responding to current events and welcoming new customers with free delivery.

items.title: Cyberattack on French supermarkets spreads to other cooling systems: tens of millions in damages
items.summary: The large-scale cyberattack on French supermarkets appears not to be limited to Danfoss refrigeration systems. Systems from Dixell and Copeland have also been affected. At E.Leclerc, employees had to clear out entire refrigerated sections, while the damage at Intermarché could…

items.title: US food watchdog outlines new rules on salt substitutes
items.summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued rules allowing manufacturers to swap salt for “safe” alternatives in everyday staples. The post US food watchdog outlines new rules on salt substitutes appeared first on Just Food .

items.title: B&G Foods sells more brands to McCall Farms
items.summary: B&G Foods has offloaded more brands to fellow McCall Farms as the company continues to streamline its portfolio and trim debt. The post B&G Foods sells more brands to McCall Farms appeared first on Just Food .

items.title: [Analysis] Amazon controls 63% of all German e-commerce, but competition is gaining ground
items.summary: Amazon controls a whopping 63% of all German e-commerce. Yet competitors are beginning to chip away at that dominance: Temu and Shein are growing at a rapid pace. Meanwhile, a new growth market is emerging: food.

items.title: Proda sees “compelling” opportunity for protein in functional drinks
items.summary: Fledgling US brand Proda is optimistic about the use of protein in functional drinks amid rising consumer demand for the nutrient in its home market.

items.title: Albert Heijn distribution centers back in operation today
items.summary: All Albert Heijn distribution centers will be back up and running by the end of the day, the retailer said in an update regarding the cyber incident that affected Ahold Delhaize. Online ordering and delivery are not yet available.

items.title: Albert Heijn Expects Distribution Centres To Be Operational Soon After Cyber Incident
items.summary: Albert Heijn said it expects its distribution centres to be operational again soon after a cyber incident temporarily disrupted operations.

items.title: Italian preserves firm Citres sells to private equity
items.summary: Citres, the family-owned, Italian, preserves business, has sold a majority of its shares to Clessidra Private Equity. The post Italian preserves firm Citres sells to private equity appeared first on Just Food .

items.title: Capturing true essence: How technology is powering modern ready-to-drink beverages
items.summary: Discerning younger consumers are reshaping ready-to-drink demand, with emphasis on natural tea, coffee and fruit flavours. Learn more here: The post Capturing true essence: How technology is powering modern ready-to-drink beverages appeared first on Just Food .

items.title: Latvia tax authority refreezes Amber Latvijas Balzams accounts
items.summary: Latvia’s State Revenue Service has reinstated a freeze on the bank accounts of spirits producer Amber Latvijas Balzams.

items.title: Sale talks for Uncle Nearest assets continue, receiver says
items.summary: Discussions on the sale of most of Uncle Nearest's assets are ongoing after a transaction with an unnamed buyer failed to materialise.

items.title: Australian watchdog launches legal action over “egg cartel”
items.summary: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has taken a dozen of the country's eggs businesses to court over alleged cartel conduct. The post Australian watchdog launches legal action over “egg cartel” appeared first on Just Food .

items.title: Albert Heijn opens its 89th Belgian store in Bilzen
items.summary: On Wednesday morning, Albert Heijn opened its 89th Belgian store in Bilzen, the 15th in the province of Limburg. For franchisee Peeters-Govers, this is the 19th store. Two more store openings are scheduled for this year.

items.title: Monster tries again on protein shakes
items.summary: The energy giant is returning to the category as innovation becomes a key piece of its growth strategy.

items.title: B&G Foods sells bean brands amid push to sharpen business
items.summary: The sale of B&M and Joan of Arc to McCall Farms marks the one-time serial acquirer’s latest divestiture as the company focuses on its core brands and pays down debt.

items.title: FDA paves the way for salt reduction in dozens of food categories
items.summary: The department will allow salt substitutes in bread, milk, condiments and other staple foods as part of an effort to reduce Americans' sodium consumption.

items.title: Biedronka And Warsaw University Launch Lab Bridging Research And Retail
items.summary: Polish retailer Biedronka and the Warsaw University of Life Sciences have launched a lab bridging research and commercial retail.

items.title: Potatoes And Tomatoes Lead French Fresh Produce Purchases - Worldpanel
items.summary: Bananas, potatoes and tomatoes dominate French fruit and vegetable purchases, according to a new study by Worldpanel by Numerator.

items.title: Sligro fears another depreciation as Belgian consumers tighten their belts
items.summary: Foodservice wholesaler Sligro continues to struggle in the Belgian market. Revenue fell by 2.2% in the third quarter, even as the company is counting on growth to improve its profitability. Sligro now expects to have to write off another portion of its Belgian goodwill by the…

items.title: How Low Can Drinkers Go? Exploring The No- And Low-Alcohol Market
items.summary: No- and low-alcohol drinks make up just a small share of the beverage market, so can they offset the decline in alcohol consumption?

items.title: Leonidas triples production capacity with a new 100-million-euro factory
items.summary: Chocolate manufacturer Leonidas is opening its new factory in Nivelles today—an investment of nearly 100 million euros that will triple its production capacity. However, the move proved more difficult and costly than expected. For the time being, the company is operating at only…

items.title: Packaging Firm Mondi Hikes Prices Again To Counter Rising Costs
items.summary: Mondi raised paper prices in Q3 to offset rising costs, with strong orders and price increases expected to support growth into 2027.

items.title: Shopping Purpose, Not Hunger, Influences Purchases, Study Finds
items.summary: A recent Breda University study challenges the notion that shopping hungry is commonly associated with making impulse purchases.
